text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to project management, especially in software development. Instead of planning everything at the start, teams work in short, focused periods called sprints, usually lasting one to four weeks. Each day begins with a quick standup meeting, where team members share what they did yesterday, what they plan to do today, and any problems they face. The project's to-do list, known as the backlog, is continuously updated with features and tasks. These tasks are often written as user stories, which describe a need from the user's perspective, such as "As a customer, I want to track my order." This iterative development allows teams to deliver small, useful parts of a project regularly, receive feedback, and adapt their plans quickly, leading to better results and higher customer satisfaction.
